lead.title: MacuMira wins MDR CE mark for its microcurrent stimulation treatment for dry AMD
lead.deck: Canada's MacuMira Medical Devices announced on Nov. 16 Class IIa CE certification (MDR 2017/745, notified body 2862) for its retinal microcurrent stimulation device, already in use in Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Its randomized sham-controlled trial published in 2023 reported 10.4 more letters of visual acuity than the sham group at 30 weeks: with dry AMD still lacking non-invasive treatments, Europe becomes the next proving ground for real-world evidence and reimbursement.

milestone.title: University of Bern spin-off PolaSight wins the Falling Walls Lab global final with its tumor-margin imager
milestone.summary: PolaOne maps tissue removed in the operating room in under a minute, label-free, using polarized light and proprietary AI models; the sample is not frozen, cut or stained and can go on intact to pathology. Founder Davide Scandella took first place in the 'tumor margins in surgery' category against 100 finalists drawn from more than 3,100 applicants.
milestone.why: Re-operations for positive margins remain one of the big hidden costs of cancer surgery, and today's frozen-section analysis destroys tissue and takes time. A very early Swiss spin-off tackling this need, now with international visibility, is exactly the profile to track ahead of its first institutional round.

deal.thesis: DCVC leads the round, joined by UC Investments, Skip Capital and Hostplus, to fund a pivotal trial with the University of California network and the FDA path for N1, an AI-driven endovascular robot that can operate on-site, remotely or autonomously. The thesis: stroke thrombectomy is limited by the scarcity of neurointerventionalists, not by technique; a remotely operable robot turns a geography problem into a software problem, a key comparable for European players Sentante and Nanoflex.

brefsEurope.title: Sofinnova closes its Crossover II fund at €725M for clinical-stage European biotech and medtech
brefsEurope.summary: Announced on Nov. 16, the fund targets clinical-stage European biopharma and medtech companies and aims to support them through to market launch. It is fresh late-stage money for the segment where European medtech is most capital-starved: the pivotal trial and the commercial launch.

brefsEurope.title: Roche Diagnostics deploys its endotrophin research prototype assay, a fibrosis biomarker, at Nordic Bioscience
brefsEurope.summary: The research immunoassay, which measures intact endotrophin released from type VI collagen, now runs on cobas e801 analyzers in the Danish company's CLIA lab for clinical trials in kidney, cardiac (HFpEF) and metabolic disease. The FDA has issued a letter supporting its use for trial enrichment; an earlier marker from the same partnership, PRO-C3, is already CE-marked.

brefsEurope.title: Ottobock becomes North American distributor for Korean WIRobotics' wearable walking robot
brefsEurope.summary: Signed on Oct. 15 and announced on Nov. 16, the deal has Otto Bock HealthCare LP selling WIM S in the U.S., online and through partner orthotic and prosthetic clinics, before a possible extension to Canada; the medical version WIM Medi will follow after regulatory authorization. The German prosthetics leader buys itself a place in consumer exoskeletons without developing one.

brefsEurope.title: Philips to nominate Todd Brinton, Edwards' chief scientific officer and Shockwave co-founder, to its Supervisory Board
brefsEurope.summary: Announced on Nov. 16 for the 2027 AGM, the nomination of this interventional cardiologist and serial founder comes alongside those of Dick Boer and Laurence Debroux, and the departure of Paul Stoffels. A signal that Philips wants a sharper eye on device innovation beyond imaging.

brefsIntl.title: Medtronic buys Contego Medical for $380M and its carotid systems with integrated embolic protection
brefsIntl.summary: Announced on Nov. 16, the deal brings in Neuroguard IEP Direct, a recently FDA-approved transcarotid revascularization system, and the Excipio thrombectomy devices; Medtronic had been a minority investor since 2020. A useful comparable: an exclusive distributor that ends up as acquirer, the typical exit scenario for vascular medtech.

brefsIntl.title: MiniMed wins FDA clearance for MiniMed Fit, its first tubeless insulin patch pump
brefsIntl.summary: The pump can be worn for up to seven days, holds 300 units and includes a meal-detection algorithm, for people with type 1 and type 2 diabetes aged seven and up; phased U.S. launch in spring 2027. Insulet, Tandem and now MiniMed are fighting over the patch: the window is closing for new hardware entrants.

brefsIntl.title: Capstan Medical performs first U.S. robot-assisted implant of its transcatheter mitral valve
brefsIntl.summary: The procedure took place on Nov. 9 at The Christ Hospital in Cincinnati, under an FDA-authorized early feasibility study, following first-in-human cases in Chile in 2025. Robotics is moving into mitral replacement, the hardest structural-heart market.

word.definition: Robots that manipulate, in place of the physician's hand, the guidewires and catheters threaded through blood vessels to place a stent or remove a clot, while the operator drives from a station shielded from X-rays, or even from another hospital.

parts.label: Control station
parts.role: the console, often haptic, from which the operator drives while seated, outside the X-ray field

parts.label: Drive unit
parts.role: mounted on the table, it pushes, pulls and rotates standard guidewires and catheters

parts.label: Software and imaging
parts.role: fuses fluoroscopy, records forces and trajectories, and lays the groundwork for AI assistance

how.t: The team sets up vascular access and loads guidewires and catheters into the robotic unit, as in a conventional procedure.
From the console, the operator navigates millimeter by millimeter under fluoroscopy; some systems even steer the wire with a magnetic field.
Angioplasty, stenting or thrombectomy are performed without a lead apron, and tomorrow remotely, to treat a stroke far from an expert center.

word.why: The first argument: literature reviews report up to a 95% cut in operator radiation exposure. But the real thesis is tele-intervention: stroke thrombectomy is limited by the number of neurointerventionalists, not by technique, hence the large recent rounds (Remedy Robotics, $62M). The first generation (Corindus, Robocath) was absorbed by industrial players; the second, largely European, is being fought on teleoperation, data and autonomy.

startups.name: Sentante
startups.use: Haptic tele-operated endovascular platform, CE-marked in May 2026, in commercial rollout in vascular surgery and interventional radiology

startups.name: Nanoflex Robotics
startups.use: ETH Zurich spin-off: ultra-flexible magnetic guidewire steered by an electromagnetic field for remote thrombectomy; EU REACT project (2026-2028) for clinical validation and approval in peripheral vascular use, then teleoperation

startups.name: Remedy Robotics
startups.use: AI-driven N1 robot (on-site, remote or autonomous); $62M Series B led by DCVC for a neurovascular pivotal trial
